content.heading: I'm John.
content.body: I'm a high school developer who likes hard technical problems. Most of what I build turns live input like a webcam feed, a voice or a news wire into something a person can act on right away. Hackathons are where I ship fastest, and a few of those builds have won.

content.heading: Saint Francis Xavier Catholic Secondary School
content.body: Senior in the IB Diploma Programme. Computer science courses: ICS3U1 and ICS4U1.

content.heading: What I'm working toward
content.body: Full-stack development with a growing AI/ML specialization. I'm most interested in systems that combine realtime interfaces, automation, voice and computer vision, and in evaluating whether AI output is actually good.

planets.title: Projects
planets.subtitle: Things I've built
planets.summary: Accessibility tooling, supply-chain intelligence, AI ad evaluation and agent security.

content.heading: Iris
content.tagline: Hands-free computer control with your eyes, mouth and voice.
content.description: An accessibility tool that turns a webcam feed and speech into full computer control, so people who can't use a mouse or keyboard can still click, scroll, switch tabs and type.
highlights: Real-time eye and mouth tracking mapped to clicks, scrolling and tab switching.
Offline speech recognition types dictated text, so motion and voice work as one interface.
Built at Hack The Valley X. Won the Future Impact category and placed 4th overall.
content.award: Hack The Valley X, Future Impact winner

content.heading: Eureka
content.tagline: Supply-chain risk intelligence on a live 3D globe.
content.description: Maps supplier and logistics exposure onto an interactive globe. It scores breaking news against a company's supplier graph and briefs decision-makers through AI voice agents they can question in plain English.
highlights: News events are scored against supplier graphs to surface exposure before it becomes a disruption.
Voice agents brief people by phone and answer follow-up questions about their risk.
Built for EurekaHacks 2026 at Waterloo's Accelerator Centre.

content.heading: Nora
content.tagline: An evaluation layer for AI-generated ad creative.
content.description: Paste a Shopify URL and Nora extracts the brand's visual DNA, then scores candidate ad images on five explainable axes and filters out off-brand variants. The same evaluator is exposed as an MCP tool so agents can grade their own work.
highlights: Pulls palette and typography from a brand's homepage and compares generated ads against real product photos.
Five explainable scoring axes instead of a single opaque number.
Built on top of Olivia (cresva.ai) and exposed to agents over MCP.

content.heading: ShieldClaw
content.tagline: Identity, policy and human approval for AI agents.
content.description: A security control plane for OpenClaw. Every AI agent gets its own machine identity, every request is checked against policy, risky actions go to a human for approval, and sensitive data is redacted before the agent sees it.
highlights: FastAPI proxy in front of OpenClaw with per-agent Auth0 identities.
Scope checks and fine-grained authorization through OpenFGA policies.
Team build that won at Hack Canada 2026.
